title: How to get your ideas to spread
speaker: Seth Godin

sentences.en: I'm going to give you four specific examples, I'm going to cover at the end about how a company called Silk tripled their sales; how an artist named Jeff Koons went from being a nobody to making a whole bunch of money and having a lot of impact;
sentences.zh: 我将给你们四个具体的例子，最后我将介绍一家名为 Silk 的公司如何将其销售额增加两倍；一位名叫杰夫·昆斯（Jeff Koons）的艺术家如何从无名小卒变成赚大钱并产生巨大影响力的人；

sentences.en: to how Frank Gehry redefined what it meant to be an architect.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克·盖里如何重新定义建筑师的意义。

sentences.en: And one of my biggest failures as a marketer in the last few years -- a record label I started that had a CD called "Sauce."
sentences.zh: 过去几年，我作为营销人员最大的失败之一是我创办了一家唱片公司，其中有一张名为“Sauce”的 CD。

sentences.en: Before I can do that I've got to tell you about sliced bread, and a guy named Otto Rohwedder.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，我必须先向您介绍一下切片面包和一个名叫奥托·罗威德 (Otto Rohwedder) 的人。

sentences.en: Now, before sliced bread was invented in the 1910s I wonder what they said?
sentences.zh: 现在，在 1910 年代切片面包发明之前，我想知道他们怎么说？

sentences.en: Like the greatest invention since the telegraph or something.
sentences.zh: 就像自电报以来最伟大的发明之类的。

sentences.en: But this guy named Otto Rohwedder invented sliced bread, and he focused, like most inventors did, on the patent part and the making part.
sentences.zh: 但是这个名叫奥托·罗韦德尔的人发明了切片面包，他像大多数发明家一样专注于专利部分和制作部分。

sentences.en: And the thing about the invention of sliced bread is this -- that for the first 15 years after sliced bread was available no one bought it; no one knew about it; it was a complete and total failure.
sentences.zh: 关于切片面包的发明，事情是这样的——在切片面包问世后的头 15 年里，没有人买它；切片面包问世后的头 15 年里，没有人买它；而切片面包问世后的头 15 年里，没有人买它。没有人知道这件事；这是彻底的失败。

sentences.en: And the reason is that until Wonder came along and figured out how to spread the idea of sliced bread, no one wanted it.
sentences.zh: 原因是，直到旺德出现并弄清楚如何传播切片面包的想法之前，没有人想要它。

sentences.en: That the success of sliced bread, like the success of almost everything we've talked about at this conference, is not always about what the patent is like, or what the factory is like -- it's about can you get your idea to spread, or not.
sentences.zh: 切片面包的成功，就像我们在这次会议上讨论的几乎所有事情的成功一样，并不总是与专利是什么样的，或者工厂是什么样的有关——而是在于你能否让你的想法传播出去。

sentences.en: And I think that the way you're going to get what you want, or cause the change that you want to change, to happen, is to figure out a way to get your ideas to spread.
sentences.zh: 我认为，要想得到你想要的东西，或者导致你想要改变的改变发生，就要找到一种方法来传播你的想法。

sentences.en: And it doesn't matter to me whether you're running a coffee shop or you're an intellectual, or you're in business, or you're flying hot air balloons.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，无论你是经营一家咖啡店，还是一个知识分子，或者你是在做生意，或者你是在驾驶热气球，这对我来说都不重要。

sentences.en: I think that all this stuff applies to everybody regardless of what we do.
sentences.zh: 我认为所有这些东西都适用于每个人，无论我们做什么。

sentences.en: That what we are living in is a century of idea diffusion.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个思想传播的世纪。

sentences.en: That people who can spread ideas, regardless of what those ideas are, win.
sentences.zh: 那些能够传播想法的人，无论这些想法是什么，都会获胜。

sentences.en: When I talk about it I usually pick business, because they make the best pictures that you can put in your presentation, and because it's the easiest sort of way to keep score.
sentences.zh: 当我谈论它时，我通常会选择商业，因为他们制作出可以放入演示文稿中的最佳图片，并且因为这是最简单的记分方式。

sentences.en: But I want you to forgive me when I use these examples because I'm talking about anything that you decide to spend your time to do.
sentences.zh: 但当我使用这些例子时，我希望您能原谅我，因为我正在谈论您决定花时间做的任何事情。

sentences.en: At the heart of spreading ideas is TV and stuff like TV.
sentences.zh: 传播思想的核心是电视和类似电视的东西。

sentences.en: TV and mass media made it really easy to spread ideas in a certain way.
sentences.zh: 电视和大众媒体使以某种方式传播思想变得非常容易。

sentences.en: I call it the "TV-industrial complex." The way the TV-industrial complex works, is you buy some ads, interrupt some people, that gets you distribution.
sentences.zh: 我称之为“电视产业综合体”。电视产业综合体的运作方式是，你购买一些广告，打断一些人的谈话，从而获得发行权。

sentences.en: You use the distribution you get to sell more products.
sentences.zh: 您可以使用获得的分销来销售更多产品。

sentences.en: You take the profit from that to buy more ads.
sentences.zh: 您可以从中获利来购买更多广告。

sentences.en: And it goes around and around and around, the same way that the military-industrial complex worked a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 它周而复始，就像很久以前军工联合体的运作方式一样。

sentences.en: That model of, and we heard it yesterday -- if we could only get onto the homepage of Google, if we could only figure out how to get promoted there, or grab that person by the throat, and tell them about what we want to do.
sentences.zh: 我们昨天听到了这种模式——如果我们只能进入谷歌的主页，如果我们只能弄清楚如何在那里晋升，或者抓住那个人的喉咙，告诉他们我们想做什么。

sentences.en: If we did that then everyone would pay attention, and we would win.
sentences.zh: 如果我们这样做，那么每个人都会关注，我们就会赢。

sentences.en: Well, this TV-industrial complex informed my entire childhood and probably yours.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这个电视工业综合体影响了我的整个童年，也可能是你的整个童年。

sentences.en: I mean, all of these products succeeded because someone figured out how to touch people in a way they weren't expecting, in a way they didn't necessarily want, with an ad, over and over again until they bought it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，所有这些产品之所以成功，是因为有人想出了如何以他们没有想到的方式，以他们不一定想要的方式，通过广告一遍又一遍地触动人们，直到他们购买为止。

sentences.en: And the thing that's happened is, they canceled the TV-industrial complex.
sentences.zh: 发生的事情是，他们取消了电视工业综合体。

sentences.en: That just over the last few years, what anybody who markets anything has discovered is that it's not working the way that it used to.
sentences.zh: 就在过去几年里，任何推销任何东西的人都发现，它不再像以前那样运作了。

sentences.en: This picture is really fuzzy, I apologize; I had a bad cold when I took it.
sentences.zh: 这张图确实很模糊，请见谅；我服用它时患了重感冒。

sentences.en: (Laughter) But the product in the blue box in the center is my poster child.
sentences.zh: （笑声）但是中间蓝色盒子里的产品是我的典型。

sentences.en: I go to the deli; I'm sick; I need to buy some medicine.
sentences.zh: 我去熟食店；我病了；我需要买一些药。

sentences.en: The brand manager for that blue product spent 100 million dollars trying to interrupt me in one year.
sentences.zh: 那个蓝色产品的品牌经理一年内花了一亿美元试图打断我。

sentences.en: 100 million dollars interrupting me with TV commercials and magazine ads and Spam and coupons and shelving allowances and spiff -- all so I could ignore every single message.
sentences.zh: 一亿美元的电视广告、杂志广告、垃圾邮件、优惠券、上架津贴和小礼物打扰了我——所有这些都是为了让我忽略每一条消息。

sentences.en: And I ignored every message because I don't have a pain reliever problem.
sentences.zh: 我忽略了每一条消息，因为我没有止痛药的问题。

sentences.en: I buy the stuff in the yellow box because I always have.
sentences.zh: 我买黄色盒子里的东西，因为我一直都有。

sentences.en: And I'm not going to invest a minute of my time to solve her problem, because I don't care.
sentences.zh: 我不会花一分钟的时间来解决她的问题，因为我不在乎。

sentences.en: Here's a magazine called "Hydrate." It's 180 pages about water.
sentences.zh: 这是一本名为“Hydrate”的杂志。这是关于水的 180 页。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Articles about water, ads about water.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 关于水的文章，关于水的广告。

sentences.en: Imagine what the world was like 40 years ago, with just the Saturday Evening Post and Time and Newsweek.
sentences.zh: 想象一下 40 年前的世界是什么样子，只有《周六晚邮报》、《时代周刊》和《新闻周刊》。

sentences.en: Now there are magazines about water. New product from Coke Japan: water salad.
sentences.zh: 现在有关于水的杂志。日本可口可乐新产品：水沙拉。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Coke Japan comes out with a new product every three weeks, because they have no idea what's going to work and what's not.
sentences.zh: （笑声）可口可乐日本公司每三周就会推出一款新产品，因为他们不知道什么有效，什么无效。

sentences.en: I couldn't have written this better myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己写得再好不过了。

sentences.en: It came out four days ago -- I circled the important parts so you can see them here.
sentences.zh: 它是四天前发布的——我圈出了重要的部分，这样你就可以在这里看到它们。

sentences.en: They've come out... Arby's is going to spend 85 million dollars promoting an oven mitt with the voice of Tom Arnold, hoping that will get people to go to Arby's and buy a roast beef sandwich.
sentences.zh: 他们出来了……Arby's 将花费 8500 万美元推广一款由汤姆·阿诺德 (Tom Arnold) 配音的烤箱手套，希望这能吸引人们去 Arby's 购买烤牛肉三明治。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Now, I had tried to imagine what could possibly be in an animated TV commercial featuring Tom Arnold, that would get you to get in your car, drive across town and buy a roast beef sandwich.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 现在，我试着想象汤姆·阿诺德主演的动画电视广告中可能会出现什么内容，它会让你开车穿过城镇，买一个烤牛肉三明治。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Now, this is Copernicus, and he was right, when he was talking to anyone who needs to hear your idea.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 现在，这是哥白尼，当他与任何需要听听你的想法的人交谈时，他是对的。

sentences.en: "The world revolves around me." Me, me, me. My favorite person -- me.
sentences.zh: “世界围着我转。”我，我，我。我最喜欢的人——我。

sentences.en: I don't want to get email from anybody; I want to get "memail."
sentences.zh: 我不想收到任何人的电子邮件；我想要收到“邮件”。

sentences.en: (Laughter) So consumers, and I don't just mean people who buy stuff at the Safeway; I mean people at the Defense Department who might buy something, or people at, you know, the New Yorker who might print your article.
sentences.zh: （笑声）所以消费者，我不仅仅指那些在 Safeway 买东西的人；还有那些在 Safeway 买东西的人。我指的是国防部的人可能会买东西，或者《纽约客》的人可能会刊登你的文章。

sentences.en: Consumers don't care about you at all; they just don't care.
sentences.zh: 消费者根本不关心你；他们只是不在乎。

sentences.en: Part of the reason is -- they've got way more choices than they used to, and way less time.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是——他们的选择比以前多得多，而时间却少得多。

sentences.en: And in a world where we have too many choices and too little time, the obvious thing to do is just ignore stuff.
sentences.zh: 在一个我们有太多选择而时间太少的世界里，显而易见的事情就是忽略一些事情。

sentences.en: And my parable here is you're driving down the road and you see a cow, and you keep driving because you've seen cows before.
sentences.zh: 我的比喻是，你在路上开车，看到一头牛，你继续开车，因为你以前见过牛。

sentences.en: Cows are invisible. Cows are boring. Who's going to stop and pull over and say -- "Oh, look, a cow."
sentences.zh: 牛是看不见的。牛很无聊。谁会停下来并说——“哦，看，一头牛。”

sentences.en: Nobody. (Laughter) But if the cow was purple -- isn't that a great special effect?
sentences.zh: 没有人。 （笑声）但是如果牛是紫色的——那不是一个很棒的特效吗？

sentences.en: I could do that again if you want. If the cow was purple, you'd notice it for a while.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话我可以再做一次。如果牛是紫色的，你会注意到它一段时间。

sentences.en: I mean, if all cows were purple you'd get bored with those, too.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果所有的牛都是紫色的，你也会对它们感到厌倦。

sentences.en: The thing that's going to decide what gets talked about, what gets done, what gets changed, what gets purchased, what gets built, is: "Is it remarkable?"
sentences.zh: 决定谈论什么、做什么、改变什么、购买什么、建造什么的因素是：“它是否引人注目？”

sentences.en: And "remarkable" is a really cool word, because we think it just means "neat," but it also means "worth making a remark about."
sentences.zh: “卓越”是一个非常酷的词，因为我们认为它只是意味着“整洁”，但它也意味着“值得发表评论”。

sentences.en: And that is the essence of where idea diffusion is going.
sentences.zh: 这就是思想传播的本质。

sentences.en: That two of the hottest cars in the United States is a 55,000-dollar giant car, big enough to hold a Mini in its trunk.
sentences.zh: 美国最热门的两辆汽车是一辆价值 55,000 美元的巨型汽车，大到足以在后备箱中容纳一辆 Mini。

sentences.en: People are paying full price for both, and the only thing they have in common is that they don't have anything in common.
sentences.zh: 人们为两者付出全价，他们唯一的共同点是他们没有任何共同点。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Every week, the number one best-selling DVD in America changes.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 美国最畅销 DVD 排行榜每周都会发生变化。

sentences.en: It's never "The Godfather," it's never "Citizen Kane," it's always some third-rate movie with some second-rate star.
sentences.zh: 它从来不是《教父》，也不是《公民凯恩》，它总是一些三流电影和一些二流明星。

sentences.en: But the reason it's number one is because that's the week it came out.
sentences.zh: 但它之所以排名第一，是因为它在那一周发布。

sentences.en: Because it's new, because it's fresh. People saw it and said "I didn't know that was there" and they noticed it.
sentences.zh: 因为它是新的，因为它是新鲜的。人们看到它并说“我不知道那儿在那里”，然后他们注意到了它。

sentences.en: Two of the big success stories of the last 20 years in retail -- one sells things that are super-expensive in a blue box, and one sells things that are as cheap as they can make them.
sentences.zh: 过去 20 年零售业的两个巨大成功故事——一个销售装在蓝色盒子里的超级昂贵的商品，一个销售尽可能便宜的商品。

sentences.en: The only thing they have in common is that they're different.
sentences.zh: 他们唯一的共同点就是不同。

sentences.en: We're now in the fashion business, no matter what we do for a living, we're in the fashion business.
sentences.zh: 我们现在从事时尚行业，无论我们以什么为生，我们都是时尚行业。

sentences.en: And people in the fashion business know what it's like to be in the fashion business -- they're used to it.
sentences.zh: 时尚界的人知道时尚界的感觉——他们已经习惯了。

sentences.en: The rest of us have to figure out how to think that way.
sentences.zh: 我们其他人必须弄清楚如何以这种方式思考。

sentences.en: How to understand that it's not about interrupting people with big full-page ads, or insisting on meetings with people.
sentences.zh: 如何理解这不是用大的整版广告打扰人们，或者坚持与人们会面。

sentences.en: But it's a totally different sort of process that determines which ideas spread, and which ones don't.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种完全不同的过程，它决定了哪些思想能够传播，哪些思想不能传播。

sentences.en: They sold a billion dollars' worth of Aeron chairs by reinventing what it meant to sell a chair.
sentences.zh: 他们通过重新定义销售椅子的含义，售出了价值 10 亿美元的 Aeron 椅子。

sentences.en: They turned a chair from something the purchasing department bought, to something that was a status symbol about where you sat at work.
sentences.zh: 他们把椅子从采购部门购买的东西变成了工作时坐姿的象征。

sentences.en: This guy, Lionel Poilâne, the most famous baker in the world -- he died two and a half months ago, and he was a hero of mine and a dear friend.
sentences.zh: 这个人，莱昂内尔·普瓦兰，世界上最著名的面包师——他在两个半月前去世了，他是我的英雄和亲爱的朋友。

sentences.en: He lived in Paris. Last year, he sold 10 million dollars' worth of French bread.
sentences.zh: 他住在巴黎。去年，他卖出了价值1000万美元的法式面包。

sentences.en: Every loaf baked in a bakery he owned, by one baker at a time, in a wood-fired oven.
sentences.zh: 每条面包都是在他拥有的面包店里用燃木烤箱一次由一位面包师烘烤的。

sentences.en: And when Lionel started his bakery, the French pooh-pooh-ed it.
sentences.zh: 当莱昂内尔开办他的面包店时，法国人对它嗤之以鼻。

sentences.en: They didn't want to buy his bread. It didn't look like "French bread."
sentences.zh: 他们不想买他的面包。它看起来不像“法式面包”。

sentences.en: It wasn't what they expected. It was neat; it was remarkable; and slowly, it spread from one person to another person until finally, it became the official bread of three-star restaurants in Paris.
sentences.zh: 这不是他们所期望的。一切都很整洁；这很了不起；慢慢地，它从一个人传到另一个人，最后成为巴黎三星级餐厅的官方面包。

sentences.en: Now he's in London, and he ships by FedEx all around the world.
sentences.zh: 现在他在伦敦，通过联邦快递运送到世界各地。

sentences.en: What marketers used to do is make average products for average people.
sentences.zh: 营销人员过去所做的就是为普通人生产普通产品。

sentences.en: That's what mass marketing is. Smooth out the edges; go for the center; that's the big market.
sentences.zh: 这就是大众营销。平滑边缘；走向中心；这就是大市场。

sentences.en: They would ignore the geeks, and God forbid, the laggards.
sentences.zh: 他们会忽视极客，但上帝禁止他们忽视落后者。

sentences.en: It was all about going for the center. But in a world where the TV-industrial complex is broken, I don't think that's a strategy we want to use any more.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是为了去中心。但在电视产业联合体支离破碎的世界里，我认为我们不再想使用这种策略。

sentences.en: I think the strategy we want to use is to not market to these people because they're really good at ignoring you.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们想要使用的策略是不向这些人推销，因为他们真的很擅长忽略你。

sentences.en: But market to these people because they care.
sentences.zh: 但向这些人推销是因为他们关心。

sentences.en: These are the people who are obsessed with something.
sentences.zh: 这些人是对某事着迷的人。

sentences.en: And when you talk to them, they'll listen, because they like listening -- it's about them.
sentences.zh: 当你和他们交谈时，他们会听，因为他们喜欢听——这是关于他们的。

sentences.en: And if you're lucky, they'll tell their friends on the rest of the curve, and it'll spread.
sentences.zh: 如果你幸运的话，他们会告诉他们的朋友在曲线的其余部分，并且它会传播。

sentences.en: It'll spread to the entire curve. They have something I call "otaku" -- it's a great Japanese word.
sentences.zh: 它将蔓延到整个曲线。他们有一种我称之为“御宅族”的东西——这是一个很棒的日语单词。

sentences.en: It describes the desire of someone who's obsessed to say, drive across Tokyo to try a new ramen noodle place, because that's what they do: they get obsessed with it.
sentences.zh: 它描述了一个痴迷于说开车穿越东京去尝试一家新拉面店的人的愿望，因为这就是他们所做的：他们对此着迷。

sentences.en: To make a product, to market an idea, to come up with any problem you want to solve that doesn't have a constituency with an otaku, is almost impossible.
sentences.zh: 制造一个产品，推销一个想法，提出任何你想解决的问题，如果没有御宅族的支持者，几乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: Instead, you have to find a group that really, desperately cares about what it is you have to say.
sentences.zh: 相反，你必须找到一个真正、极度关心你要说的话的团体。

sentences.en: Talk to them and make it easy for them to tell their friends.
sentences.zh: 与他们交谈，让他们轻松告诉他们的朋友。

sentences.en: There's a hot sauce otaku, but there's no mustard otaku.
sentences.zh: 有辣酱宅男，但没有芥末宅男。

sentences.en: That's why there's lots and lots of kinds of hot sauces, and not so many kinds of mustard.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么辣酱的种类有很多很多，而芥末的种类却没有那么多。

sentences.en: Not because it's hard to make interesting mustard -- you could make interesting mustard -- but people don't, because no one's obsessed with it, and thus no one tells their friends.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为制作有趣的芥末很难——你可以制作有趣的芥末——而是人们不这样做，因为没有人对它着迷，因此没有人告诉他们的朋友。

sentences.en: Krispy Kreme has figured this whole thing out.
sentences.zh: Krispy Kreme 已经解决了这一切。

sentences.en: It has a strategy, and what they do is, they enter a city, they talk to the people, with the otaku, and then they spread through the city to the people who've just crossed the street.
sentences.zh: 它有一个策略，他们所做的就是进入一个城市，与人们交谈，与御宅族交谈，然后他们在城市中传播给刚刚过马路的人们。

sentences.en: This yoyo right here cost 112 dollars, but it sleeps for 12 minutes.
sentences.zh: 这里的悠悠球售价 112 美元，但它可以休眠 12 分钟。

sentences.en: Not everybody wants it but they don't care.
sentences.zh: 不是每个人都想要它，但他们不在乎。

sentences.en: They want to talk to the people who do, and maybe it'll spread.
sentences.zh: 他们想与那些这样做的人交谈，也许它会传播开来。

sentences.en: These guys make the loudest car stereo in the world.
sentences.zh: 这些人制造了世界上最响亮的汽车音响。

sentences.en: (Laughter) It's as loud as a 747 jet. You can't get in, the car's got bulletproof glass, because it'll blow out the windshield otherwise.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 声音和 747 喷气式飞机一样大声。你不能进去，车上有防弹玻璃，否则挡风玻璃就会被炸飞。

sentences.en: But the fact remains that when someone wants to put a couple of speakers in their car, if they've got the otaku or they've heard from someone who does, they go ahead and they pick this.
sentences.zh: 但事实仍然是，当有人想在他们的车里放几个扬声器时，如果他们有御宅族或者他们听说有人这么做，他们就会选择这个。

sentences.en: It's really simple -- you sell to the people who are listening, and just maybe, those people tell their friends.
sentences.zh: 这真的很简单——你把产品卖给那些正在倾听的人，也许这些人会告诉他们的朋友。

sentences.en: So when Steve Jobs talks to 50,000 people at his keynote, who are all tuned in from 130 countries watching his two-hour commercial -- that's the only thing keeping his company in business -- it's that those 50,000 people care desperately enough
sentences.zh: 因此，当史蒂夫·乔布斯在他的主题演讲中与 50,000 人交谈时，他们都从 130 个国家收看他的两小时商业广告——这是让他的公司继续营业的唯一因素——那就是这 50,000 人非常关心

sentences.en: to watch a two-hour commercial, and then tell their friends.
sentences.zh: 观看两个小时的广告，然后告诉他们的朋友。

sentences.en: Pearl Jam, 96 albums released in the last two years.
sentences.zh: Pearl Jam，近两年发行了 96 张专辑。

sentences.en: Every one made a profit. How? They only sell them on their website.
sentences.zh: 每个人都获利了。如何？他们只在他们的网站上出售。

sentences.en: Those people who buy them have the otaku, and then they tell their friends, and it spreads and it spreads.
sentences.zh: 那些购买它们的人都是御宅族，然后他们告诉他们的朋友，它就蔓延开来。

sentences.en: This hospital crib cost 10,000 dollars, 10 times the standard.
sentences.zh: 这个医院婴儿床花费了1万美元，是标准的10倍。

sentences.en: But hospitals are buying it faster than any other model.
sentences.zh: 但医院购买它的速度比任何其他型号都快。

sentences.en: Hard Candy nail polish, doesn't appeal to everybody, but to the people who love it, they talk about it like crazy.
sentences.zh: 硬糖指甲油，并不是对所有人都有吸引力，但对于喜欢它的人来说，他们会疯狂地谈论它。

sentences.en: This paint can right here saved the Dutch Boy paint company, making them a fortune.
sentences.zh: 这个油漆罐拯救了荷兰男孩油漆公司，让他们发了财。

sentences.en: It costs 35 percent more than regular paint because Dutch Boy made a can that people talk about, because it's remarkable.
sentences.zh: 它比普通油漆贵 35%，因为 Dutch Boy 制造的罐子令人津津乐道，因为它非常出色。

sentences.en: They didn't just slap a new ad on the product; they changed what it meant to build a paint product.
sentences.zh: 他们不只是在产品上打了一个新广告；他们改变了制造涂料产品的意义。

sentences.en: AmIhotornot.com -- everyday 250,000 people go to this site, run by two volunteers, and I can tell you they are hard graders -- (Laughter)
sentences.zh: AmIhotornot.com——每天有 250,000 人访问这个由两名志愿者运营的网站，我可以告诉你他们都是努力评分的人——（笑声）

sentences.en: They didn't get this way by advertising a lot.
sentences.zh: 他们并不是通过大量广告才达到这个目的的。

sentences.en: They got this way by being remarkable, sometimes a little too remarkable.
sentences.zh: 他们之所以能取得这样的成就，是因为他们表现出色，有时甚至有点过于出色。

sentences.en: And this picture frame has a cord going out the back, and you plug it into the wall.
sentences.zh: 这个相框的背面有一根电线，你可以将它插入墙上。

sentences.en: My father has this on his desk, and he sees his grandchildren everyday, changing constantly.
sentences.zh: 我父亲的桌子上有这个，他每天都会看到他的孙子们，不断地变化。

sentences.en: And every single person who walks into his office hears the whole story of how this thing ended up on his desk.
sentences.zh: 每个走进他办公室的人都会听到这东西如何出现在他办公桌上的整个故事。

sentences.en: And one person at a time, the idea spreads.
sentences.zh: 一次一个人，这个想法就会传播开来。

sentences.en: These are not diamonds, not really. They're made from "cremains."
sentences.zh: 这些不是钻石，不是真正的钻石。它们是由“骨灰”制成的。

sentences.en: After you're cremated you can have yourself made into a gem.
sentences.zh: 火化后，您可以将自己打造成宝石。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Oh, you like my ring? It's my grandmother.
sentences.zh: （笑声）哦，你喜欢我的戒指吗？这是我的祖母。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Fastest-growing business in the whole mortuary industry.
sentences.zh: （笑声）整个太平间行业中增长最快的业务。

sentences.en: But you don't have to be Ozzie Osborne -- you don't have to be super-outrageous to do this.
sentences.zh: 但你不必成为奥齐·奥斯本——你不必非常离谱才能做到这一点。

sentences.en: What you have to do is figure out what people really want and give it to them.
sentences.zh: 你要做的就是弄清楚人们真正想要什么并给予他们。

sentences.en: A couple of quick rules to wrap up. The first one is: Design is free when you get to scale.
sentences.zh: 总结一些快速规则。第一个是：当你达到规模时，设计是免费的。

sentences.en: The people who come up with stuff that's remarkable more often than not figure out how to put design to work for them.
sentences.zh: 那些想出非凡作品的人往往会弄清楚如何让设计为他们所用。

sentences.en: Number two: The riskiest thing you can do now is be safe.
sentences.zh: 第二：你现在能做的最危险的事情就是保证安全。

sentences.en: Proctor and Gamble knows this, right? The whole model of being Proctor and Gamble is always about average products for average people.
sentences.zh: 宝洁公司知道这一点，对吗？宝洁公司的整个模式始终是为普通人提供普通产品。

sentences.en: That's risky. The safe thing to do now is to be at the fringes, be remarkable.
sentences.zh: 那是有风险的。现在最安全的做法就是站在边缘，表现出色。

sentences.en: And being very good is one of the worst things you can possibly do.
sentences.zh: 而变得非常优秀是你可能做的最糟糕的事情之一。

sentences.en: Very good is boring. Very good is average.
sentences.zh: 很好就是无聊。非常好就是平均水平。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter whether you're making a record album, or you're an architect, or you have a tract on sociology.
sentences.zh: 无论你是在制作唱片，还是建筑师，或者你有社会学方面的知识，这都无关紧要。

sentences.en: If it's very good, it's not going to work, because no one's going to notice it.
sentences.zh: 如果它非常好，它就不会起作用，因为没有人会注意到它。

sentences.en: So my three stories. Silk put a product that does not need to be in the refrigerated section next to the milk in the refrigerated section.
sentences.zh: 所以我的三个故事。 Silk将不需要冷藏区的产品放在冷藏区的牛奶旁边。

sentences.en: Sales tripled. Why? Milk, milk, milk -- not milk.
sentences.zh: 销售额增加了两倍。为什么？牛奶，牛奶，牛奶——不是牛奶。

sentences.en: For the people who were there and looking at that section, it was remarkable.
sentences.zh: 对于在场观看该部分的人来说，这是非凡的。

sentences.en: They didn't triple their sales with advertising; they tripled it by doing something remarkable.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有通过广告将销售额增加两倍；而是通过广告来实现销售额的增长。他们通过做一些非凡的事情将其增加了两倍。

sentences.en: That is a remarkable piece of art. You don't have to like it, but a 40-foot tall dog made out of bushes in the middle of New York City is remarkable.
sentences.zh: 这是一件非凡的艺术品。你不一定要喜欢它，但一只 40 英尺高的狗在纽约市中心的灌木丛中制成，确实很了不起。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Frank Gehry didn't just change a museum; he changed an entire city's economy by designing one building that people from all over the world went to see.
sentences.zh: （笑声）弗兰克·盖里不仅改变了博物馆，还改变了博物馆。他设计了一栋吸引世界各地人们前来参观的建筑，从而改变了整个城市的经济。

sentences.en: Now, at countless meetings at, you know, the Portland City Council, or who knows where, they said, we need an architect -- can we get Frank Gehry?
sentences.zh: 现在，在波特兰市议会的无数次会议上，或者谁知道在哪里，他们说，我们需要一位建筑师——我们能找到弗兰克·盖里吗？

sentences.en: Because he did something that was at the fringes.
sentences.zh: 因为他做了一些边缘的事情。

sentences.en: And my big failure? I came out with an entire -- (Music) A record album and hopefully a whole bunch of record albums in SACD, this remarkable new format -- and I marketed it straight to people with 20,000-dollar stereos.
sentences.zh: 而我的重大失败呢？我推出了一张完整的——（音乐）唱片专辑，希望还有一大堆 SACD 唱片，这种非凡的新格式——我直接向拥有 20,000 美元立体声音响的人们推销它。

sentences.en: People with 20,000-dollar stereos don't like new music.
sentences.zh: 拥有两万美元立体声音响的人不喜欢新音乐。

sentences.en: (Laughter) So what you need to do is figure out who does care.
sentences.zh: （笑声）所以你需要做的是弄清楚谁在乎。

sentences.en: Who is going to raise their hand and say, "I want to hear what you're doing next," and sell something to them.
sentences.zh: 谁会举手说：“我想听听你接下来要做什么”，然后向他们出售一些东西。

sentences.en: The last example I want to give you. This is a map of Soap Lake, Washington.
sentences.zh: 我想给你们举最后一个例子。这是华盛顿州肥皂湖的地图。

sentences.en: As you can see, if that's nowhere, it's in the middle of it.
sentences.zh: 正如您所看到的，如果它不存在，那么它就在中间。

sentences.en: (Laughter) But they do have a lake. And people used to come from miles around to swim in the lake.
sentences.zh: （笑声）但他们确实有一个湖。人们过去常常从几英里远的地方来到湖里游泳。

sentences.en: They don't anymore. So the founding fathers said, "We've got some money to spend.
sentences.zh: 他们不再这样做了。所以开国元勋们说：“我们有一些钱可以花。

sentences.en: What can we build here?" And like most committees, they were going to build something pretty safe.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在这里建造什么？”和大多数委员会一样，他们将建立一些非常安全的东西。

sentences.en: And then an artist came to them -- this is a true artist's rendering -- he wants to build a 55-foot tall lava lamp in the center of town.
sentences.zh: 然后一位艺术家来找他们——这是真正的艺术家的渲染——他想在镇中心建造一盏55英尺高的熔岩灯。

sentences.en: That's a purple cow; that's something worth noticing.
sentences.zh: 那是一头紫色的牛；这是值得注意的事情。

sentences.en: I don't know about you, but if they build it, that's where I'm going to go.
sentences.zh: 我不了解你，但如果他们建造了它，那就是我要去的地方。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for your attention.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您的关注。
